liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): Stella Blue into Goin' Down The Road is called great; Jerry struggles to find the phrasing in places [15][17]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (1 review): The Lazy Lightnin' into Supplication pairing is singled out as great [12]
- **Sunrise** (1 review): Reviewer dislikes Sunrise being played; otherwise would rate the show higher [18]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Described as weird and trippy, and part of the late-show run that crushes [12]
- **Around And Around** (1 review): Reviewer considers it among the hottest versions heard from any era, with Donna hitting her marks [17]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): The encore starts with Weir chuckling a harmony in the lyric, then the band drives it home [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-10-28.sbd.miller.96159.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 180 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1977-10-28.148907.betty-board.anon.noel.t-flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 181 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd77-10-28.sbd.munder.8520.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 179 min; rated 4.17/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: The opening of the first song is clipped on this soundboard copy; Reviewer ranks it among the ten best-sounding Dead recordings found while searching the archive; Reviewer finds the sound not especially crisp [8][14][15]
- **gd1977-10-28.sonyECM990.minches.96569.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 169 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [6]. Said about its sound: Tape speed varied throughout, so nearly every song needed pitch correction [6]

## Around the show

- A crowd member can be heard shouting "Yea" repeatedly throughout the whole recording [15]
- Reviewer finds the show representative of 1977 as a whole [7]
- The Not Fade Away > Stella Blue > Goin' Down The Road sequence reportedly occurred only twice ever [11]
- Not as big as the monster 1977 shows, but comparable to the Oklahoma show [12]
- Show has highs and lows; other 1977 shows are considered stronger [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-10-28.sbd.miller.96159.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat [1]. Also: An audience-source patch at the end of Around And Around is used in this restored Betty Board; Source chain: Sony ECM-990 to cassette master to reel to CD; Patches cover the first 22 seconds of The Promised Land and part of Around And Around, from David Minches' source [1][17]
- **gd1977-10-28.148907.betty-board.anon.noel.t-flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Source & Transfer by Anonymous;Edited & Mastered using Adobe Audition by Joe Noel; source: Betty SBD > Reel Master > PCM > pcm clone [2]. Also: Source was shared anonymously, and the reel came from Bob Wagner [2]
- **gd77-10-28.sbd.munder.8520.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Circulates as a Betty Board soundboard recording; Betty Board chain via Jens Tilsner, then seeded to etree by Willy [3][7]
- **gd1977-10-28.sonyECM990.minches.96569.flac16**: transferred by David Minches; source: Sony ECM-990 -> Cassette Master [6]. Also: Taped on a Sony ECM-990 with the reel supplied by Bob Wagner; Joe B. Jones did pitch correction [6]
